correctness.rationale: Starting from the published exact SQN formulation, the proof eliminates the fifth and fourth partition choices by linear optimization, then maximizes the remaining concave quadratic/cubic branches. The only near-critical branch is reduced to a normalized function whose stationary envelope is proved decreasing for a/b>=1/4 by exact discriminant and polynomial-sign calculations. The complementary branch is bounded by q^6/16, below the explicit Kq^6 threshold. The integer lower construction reaches at least Kq^6 for every q>=10, forcing the exact Blackburn maximum. The packaged exact verifier reproduces all algebraic constants and independently checks SQN instances without being used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim resolves a named 2013 eventual-optimality conjecture in the first unsolved even length beyond the short exact cases, over an infinite alphabet-size tail rather than an arbitrary finite slice. It converts a computationally difficult integer optimization into a closed exact formula and gives a concrete threshold q>=10. This is structurally informative because the neighboring q=9 optimization is known to exhibit a rounding exception, so the theorem identifies where the asymptotic one-boundary geometry becomes provably dominant.
